learning_outcomes.text: Acquire the method and knowledge required to describe, understand and design industrial production and storage systems, and to define their maintenance criteria; efficiently use project management tools by means of statistical basics. Learn the structure and operating principles of industrial plants in terms of: organization and management of raw material transformation into finished products, reliability of complex systems, role of human resources and industrial automation, production flows and layout, KPI, and performance measurements.

Apply acquired knowledge in a real design context, as well as in multidisciplinary or non-familiar areas. Specifically, apply knowledge to the industrialization of a production process, from feasibility study to defining the best production structure and management, assessing automation possibilities, and controlling the process through KPIs.

Understand and critically evaluate the main production systems (forced and non-forced technological processes, production or assembly, manual or automated); use acquired knowledge to analyze existing systems, assess their performances and adequacy, evaluate the impact of strategic, planning, and operational decisions, and measure plant performances.

Acquire specific vocabulary inherent to production plants. Communicate the main contents of the course, both written and orally, such as ideas, engineering issues, and related solutions. Communicate knowledge through appropriate tools, solving numerical problems using common industry methods such as tables, diagrams, flow charts, and numerical spreadsheets.
Deepen knowledge of production plants through autonomous consultation of specialized books, scientific or divulgative journals, even outside the topics explained during lectures.

syllabus_topics: Impact of automation on manufacturing and assembly processes
Theory of reliability for the maintenance of production systems

assessment_methods.method: Written test based on open questions

assessment_rules: Verification takes place through a written test based on open questions, lasting 2.5 hours, usually consisting of 11/12 questions. Theoretical demonstrations have a weight of 1.0; Plant design and technical drawings weight 1.5; Exercises weight 1.8. The final vote is calculated by assigning a mark in the range 0-30 for each question and then performing the weighted average of the individual evaluations, with final ceiling to the next unit. The test is exceeded if it reaches a score of at least 18 points. "30 cum laude" is given to students who achieve the highest score on each item and use precise vocabulary.
